第 96 章 Yes, Code Wins Arguments. But Why? And How to Be Polite About It是的，代码赢得争论。但为什么？以及怎么礼貌地做

Joe Dunn / 乔·邓恩

— 第 262 页 —

OK, so when to stop meeting and write some code? This came up while working with a senior software engineer recently. He had diligently gone to the project meetings, tried to move things forward, tried to drive consensus, but things were stuck. He knew in his bones that more meetings wouldn't help, but a week of him coding a prototype would. But he didn't want to "take the project away," or appear arrogant and pushy. (All good concerns…). What to do?

好，那什么时候停止会议写代码？这最近和一个高级软件工程师合作时出现。他认真参加项目会议，试图推进事情，试图推动共识，但事情卡住了。他骨子里知道更多会议没用，但他写一周原型会有用。但他不想「把项目拿走」，或显得傲慢和强势。（都是好的顾虑……）怎么办？

"Code wins arguments" has been around for a while. This is from the Facebook S1 filing: "Instead of debating for days whether a new idea is possible or what the best way to build something is, hackers would rather just prototype something and see what works." Classic! "Hackers would rather…." Of course they would! No more stupid meetings, we're just going to build it and you guys can sort it out later! Cool! The implied context is an argument and the outcome is a win for the hackers—which means a defeat for somebody else. Here's the thing though: "Code wins arguments" is shorthand for a much more subtle process. Software is a creative act. When we're thinking about building a piece of software, we don't know how it's going to turn out. We really don't. We can speculate, sketch potential structures and collective outlines of what we think we're going to build, but until we start to build it, we won't know.

「代码赢得争论」已经存在一段时间了。这来自 Facebook S1 招股书：「与其辩论好几天一个新想法是否可能或构建某物的最佳方式是什么，黑客宁愿直接原型化一些东西看什么有效。」经典！「黑客宁愿……」他们当然愿意！没有更多愚蠢会议，我们只是要建它，你们以后可以理清楚！酷！隐含上下文是争论，结果是黑客的胜利——这意味着别人的失败。但事情是：「代码赢得争论」是一个微妙得多的过程的简写。软件是创造性行为。当我们想构建一个软件时，我们不知道它会变成什么样。我们真的不知道。我们可以推测、勾勒我们认为要建的潜在结构和集体大纲，但在开始构建之前，我们不会知道。

— 第 263 页 —

The best way of putting this came from a young entrepreneur I was working with a while ago. We were staring at a design for a new product. It looked good, but something was bothering both of us. Finally, he said, "We need to build it. We don't know what it wants to be yet". In every creative process I know, there is a balance between the fine, subtle details of the actual work, and the elegance and structure of the final goal we have in mind. They inform one another. You can analyze the structure of a Mozart symphony all you want—if you don't have Mozart's command of the details, you ain't gonna write one. And if you start a novel or a software project without a good idea of the structure, after you get about a third of the way in, you'll find yourself in a tar pit—too many possibilities, too many threads that don't tie together. A mess. So, the phrase "Code wins arguments" is, I think, blunt engineering shorthand for "we need to go and create now, and see what this thing we're building wants to be". It's a necessary step in the creative process.

最好的说法来自我之前合作的一个年轻创业者。我们盯着一个新产品的设计。它看起来不错，但有什么在困扰我们两个。最后他说：「我们需要建它。我们还不知道它想成为什么。」在我知道的每个创造性过程中，实际工作的精细微妙细节和我们心中最终目标的优雅结构之间有平衡。它们互相启发。你可以想分析莫扎特交响曲的结构就分析——如果你没有莫扎特对细节的掌控，你写不出一首。如果你开始一部小说或软件项目时没有好的结构想法，在你走了大约三分之一后，你会发现自己在焦油坑里——太多可能性，太多不连在一起的线。一团糟。所以，「代码赢得争论」这个短语，我认为，是「我们需要现在去创造，看看我们在建的这个东西想成为什么」的生硬工程简写。它是创造性过程中必要的一步。

It does mean that for some period, the project is no longer a team sport—it's in the hands of a few (maybe one) engineers. So, there's some letting go necessary here. The rest of the team has to understand that the product won't show itself until some code gets written. But it's also true that the wider team isn't out of the picture forever, or loses ownership. The step after coding a prototype is getting back together, seeing what's beginning to show itself, and fit it into the wider structure of the business. Ideally in a software company, the idea that software needs periods of "just finding out" is baked in. If so, great. "We need to go and code our way through this" is an accepted stage in the process. If not, you need to get there—change the culture, which we know takes a while, and a lot of repetition.

这确实意味着一段时间内，项目不再是团队运动——它在少数（可能一个）工程师手中。所以这里需要一些放手。团队其他人必须理解产品在写一些代码之前不会展现自己。但同样真实的是更宽的团队不会永远出局，或失去所有权。写原型后的步骤是重新聚在一起，看什么开始展现出来，把它适配进业务的更宽结构。理想情况下在软件公司，软件需要「只是探索」时期的理念是烤进去的。如果是，太好了。「我们需要走代码路通过这个」是过程中被接受的阶段。如果不是，你需要到达那里——改变文化，我们知道这需要时间和很多重复。

— 第 264 页 —

So how to communicate this to the team? How could the engineer I was working with get out of the jam? Well, we can ask the Magic Question: "What do they want?" My guess is they don't want to sit in fruitless meetings for hours. My guess is that they would like the project to move forward, like, now. My guess is they don't want to lose ownership. So, communicate a solution: "in a week, I can show you a prototype that does X and we'll know where to go". Or: "in two, this feature will be up and running and we can see if anybody wants it". Time-box it, make it clear it's an exploration and that it supports the project as a whole. "Code wins arguments" implies an argument and a defeat. "Code moves us all forward" might be a better, although less pithy, approach to bring to the work. Software is a creative process. Sometimes it needs to tell us what it wants to be. Your development culture needs to acknowledge that.

那怎么和团队沟通？和我合作的工程师怎么走出困境？我们可以问魔法问题：「他们想要什么？」我猜他们不想坐在无果的会议里几小时。我猜他们想项目前进，比如现在。我猜他们不想失去所有权。所以沟通一个解决方案：「一周内，我可以给你看一个做 X 的原型，我们就知道往哪走」。或者：「两周内，这个功能会跑起来，我们可以看有没有人想要它」。时间盒它，说清楚这是探索、它支持整个项目。「代码赢得争论」暗示争论和失败。「代码推动我们所有人前进」可能是一个更好、虽然没那么精辟的工作方式。软件是创造性过程。有时候它需要告诉我们它想成为什么。你的开发文化需要承认这一点。
